reasoning_traces.think:
A world model encodes the joint distribution p(s, a, r) over states, actions, and rewards, where s ∈ S, a ∈ A, r ∈ R. The core operator is the transition kernel p(s_{t+1}|s_t,a_t), which defines how the environment evolves under agent behavior. This kernel is typically parameterized by a neural network and trained via maximum likelihood or reinforcement learning objectives. Generative likelihood p(x|z) links observations x to latent codes z, forming a variational autoencoder framework. Latent dynamics p(z_{t+1}|z_t,a_t) define how internal representations evolve. These components interlock: GSI uses the generative likelihood to decode inputs into latent states, while GSE employs the transition kernel to simulate future scenarios. The failure mode occurs when the model's assumptions about Markovianity or stationarity break down due to non-stationary environments or distributional shift.
